account:
I have mostly followed my ordinary appointments today: market, lunch, accounts, tea with my neighbour, and now the office. The secretary reported no correspondence, accounts figures, or requests requiring a decision earlier today. I have asked for a financial summary and a record of local news, but have not yet received an intelligible new report since returning.

The one rumour I investigated concerned a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' My neighbour attributed those words to Townsfolk Two, outside the bakery this morning. When pressed, the reported evidence was only the baker carrying wheat and lights at the bakery. I also heard Townsfolk 30 say the baker was carrying wheat. The neighbour says the baker described his work as ordinary fresh-bread baking and knew of no special occasion. None of this establishes any bridge work, port project, or unusual gathering. My neighbour personally saw no interesting visitors or dockside gathering today. They suggested a bench by the landing, explicitly as their own wish, not an existing project.

Now the innkeeper has directly invited me to the great hall tomorrow at eighteen for a brief 'community hospitality presentation.' This is the clearest new development. I do not yet know who else is involved or what the presentation contains. It might simply concern hospitality or a community event; I have no evidence connecting it to the bakery rumour. I am curious whether it explains my feeling that something is happening without me, but that remains speculation. I should ask the innkeeper about its purpose and have the secretary record the appointment if I accept.
